title: Route apps + discover through the selected daemon/transport path
description:
WHAT: Route every CLI LAN read through the selected path. Two unwired call sites found during 2026-10-14 live verification (binary 92cbdf7, sha256 eec1ea3f...b583cf22):

CLI-direct and never consults daemon_client, while sibling read verbs info/active-app route through the daemon (0b162d9). Live result: `apps 192.168.1.182` fails in-pane with EHOSTUNREACH yet exits 0 with a 37-row list via ssh-localhost tree; ZESTROKU_DAEMON_URL has no effect on it.
(b) crates/zestroku-cli/src/devices.rs:133 calls discover(&AsupersyncTransport, ...) directly, bypassing send_selected, so the SSDP/discover path ignores ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=std.

[b] `ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=std zestroku devices` (SSDP path) honors the selector; planted negative: `ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=bogus` refuses or falls back deterministically, never silently uses asupersync.
EVIDENCE: live legs 2026-10-14 (devices L1+L2 exit 0, info/active-app exit 0, apps exit 0 via ssh tree / exit 1 in-pane, key denial exit 4 audit 6 zero dispatch); scratch var/agent-tmp/livelegs-local/apps-ssh.out (37 rows), apps.out (exit-1 note).

title: CLI and MCP reach devices through the resident daemon (agent panes cannot open LAN sockets)
description:
WHAT: (a) CLI verbs (devices, info, active-app, apps, key, launch) send to the resident daemon over loopback when it is up and connect directly only with ZESTROKU_DIRECT=1; (b) the MCP stdio server started by an agent is a client of the daemon and opens no LAN socket itself; (c) typed errors: DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE (daemon down: exit within 2 s, no hang) and LAN_BLOCKED_BY_OS_POLICY (a direct connect fails with errno 65 / EHOSTUNREACH while the host answers ping or a platform tool).
WHY: on 2026-10-10 every LAN connect from agent-pane process trees failed with errno 65 while the same binary worked under sshd (measured by PeachKnoll at 22:10Z, reproduced by three agents; mechanism inferred to be macOS Local Network privacy per process tree). An MCP stdio server is spawned by the agent, so it sits in that same blocked tree: a stdio MCP that connects to Rokus itself would be unusable by exactly the agents it is for. The m7c design (c) has this flaw.

title: zestroku doctrine root: owner rules + scope boundary
description:
Root doctrine bead for the zestroku product. Carries the owner rules and the scope boundary every other bead inherits (plan §2/§8):

- Own devices + own LAN only (Express 4K+ .182-class, 50RokuTV .222-class). Never a device the owner does not control.
- Mutations (keypress/launch/install, any settings change) are human-led: one approval per op at point of use. No standing blanket.
- Never commit identifiers (serial/UDN/MAC/ad-id), captures, keys, or firmware images. Fixtures are scrubbed (FIXTURESERIAL-class placeholders).
- Never flash a device. Firmware lane = download + static parse only, offline.
- Documentation-style wording in all instructional text.
- No fuzzing of the shared household LAN in a way that degrades it; cap rates; bench-preferred.
- Shared-tree discipline: Agent Mail reservations before edits; `git commit --only` reserved paths; implementer != verifier (kit-close-needs-evidence).
- Builds/tests via rch (RCH_WORKER=contabo-1 RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1). No darwin workers. CI never needs the network: sim e2e instead.

Acceptance: every other zestroku bead closed with cited evidence; this bead closes last.

title: Human-bound confirmation: tokens an agent cannot mint for itself (bound to device, verb, args, expiry)
description:
WHAT: (a) `zestroku approve <verb> <device> <args...>`, run by the owner, prints a single-use token bound to (device, verb, args, 5-minute expiry); (b) the gate verifies the binding and consumes the token (token store in the action DB); a blank or free-text token, a token for other args or another device, an expired token and a reused token are all refused and audited; (c) `approve` requires an interactive TTY and a typed phrase; in daemon mode the owner approves through an owner-only channel (the loopback web remote or similar): channel choice is an owner decision.
WHY: plan section 1: "an agent doing something careless at 2 a.m. is the failure to design against". Today `--confirm <any non-blank string>` passes (the 2026-10-10 live leg used `--confirm jr`), so an agent can confirm its own mutation; the confirmation is a speed bump, not a guard. The same limit applies to any token that binds bytes but not identity.
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] [a] `approve launch <dev> 12` prints a token that the gate accepts for exactly that action once.
- [ ] [b] planted negatives, each exit 4 with a denied audit row and zero POSTs in the request log: the token for 12 used for 13; used for another device; used after expiry (injected clock); used twice; a blank token; a free-text token.
- [ ] [c] `approve` without a TTY refuses with exit 2; the existing `--confirm <anything>` path is removed (planted negative: re-adding it turns a test red).
NO-CLAIM: cannot stop an agent with the same OS account that deliberately drives a TTY (for example tmux send-keys); it stops accidental and self-served confirmations and binds approval to the exact action.

title: Report serve readiness only after bind and drain on SIGINT
description:
WHAT: (a) Emit the serve listening/readiness line only after the HTTP listener bind succeeds; a port-conflict launch must exit nonzero without claiming readiness. (b) Route SIGINT through the same orderly listener shutdown path as SIGTERM; an actual loopback daemon must exit successfully and release its port after SIGINT. Keep existing SIGTERM in-flight drain acceptance owned by .1.1.
WHY: Current serve.rs:45-47 registers SIGTERM only, while :120 prints listening before runtime.block_on starts the listener at :121. Frankensonos latest daemon waits for listener readiness before announcing it and handles both SIGINT and SIGTERM. False readiness misleads service supervision; default Ctrl-C termination can bypass shutdown hooks.
ACCEPTANCE: [a] In-tree real-binary tests reserve a loopback port, prove bind failure emits no listening line, and prove successful ready state only after /health responds; no sleep-only readiness. title: M7d: durable store in zestroku-core (tables + migrations + round-trip proof)
description:
Store bead (plan §5 P5 M7d, §3 schema): the durable store in zestroku-core.

Tables (append-only migration list, frankensonos §7 pattern):
- devices(id TEXT PK, name, ip, model, model_num, firmware, wifi_driver, access_tier, last_seen INT)
- apps(device_id, app_id, name, version, fetched_at INT, PK(device_id, app_id))
- capabilities(device_id, cap, PK(device_id, cap))
- access_tier(device_id TEXT PK, tier, probe_at INT, probe_map TEXT) — open/403/404/untested per command class
- actions(id INTEGER PK, at, client, surface, intent, decision, result, before_state) — M4/M7e consumes this

Known hazard (frankensonos §4 item 3): fsqlite engine futures overflow a default thread stack — AsyncConnection-style handle or Box::pin on a dedicated 32MiB thread; never a raw !Send future on a default stack. title: M7f: zestroku-sim — virtual devices on loopback (CI-verifiable e2e)
description:
Sim bead (plan §12.4, frankensonos §12.4 analog — LOAD-BEARING here): crates/zestroku-sim, virtual Roku devices on real localhost sockets.

Why mandatory: rch build workers have no speaker LAN; without the sim there is no CI-verifiable e2e path at all. No mocks where a real socket works (AGENTS.md).

Scope:
- Per-virtual-device localhost HTTP server (asupersync h1 listener, HostPolicy::allow_list per the FND-DEPS hazard): device-info XML from scrubbed fixtures (FIXTURESERIAL-class placeholders), query/active-app, query/apps, query/media-player state machines.
- Tier mode reproducing the Limited 403 map exactly (40-byte body 'ECP command not allowed in Limited mode.') so tier-gate tests run against both tiers.
- keypress focus-state transitions and launch active-app transitions; tv-active-channel only on the virtual TV (the §4 fingerprint).
- Fault injection: latency, connection refusal (suspend), IP-change scenario.
- zestroku sim --scenario two-devices runs the §1 workflows; the e2e suite drives the real zestroku binary against it, logging each command/response as JSON lines.

- [ ] e2e suite runs on rch workers (no LAN) covering devices/info/apps/key/launch against the sim
- [ ] Limited-tier sim reproduces the exact 403 body/headers from the wire doc; parser tests pass against it
- [ ] fault injection: unreachable-device retry path exercised (§12.14 pre-work)
- [ ] ZESTROKU_E2E_LIVE=1 lane documented (live opt-in, never CI)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] e2e suite runs on rch workers (no LAN) covering devices/info/apps/key/launch against the sim
- [ ] Limited-tier sim reproduces the exact 403 body/headers from the wire doc; parser tests pass against it
- [ ] fault injection: unreachable-device retry path exercised (§12.14 pre-work)
- [ ] ZESTROKU_E2E_LIVE=1 lane documented (live opt-in, never CI)

## AMENDMENT 2026-10-10 (director, reality-check R1)
Planted negatives (added): [ ] flipping one byte of the Limited 403 body turns the byte-exact test red; [ ] a router returning 403 under Permissive turns the wrapper-not-filter test red (the should_panic case); [ ] a POST that slips past the gate shows up in the request-log assertion and turns it red.
Decision recorded: GET /keypress/* and /launch/* follow ECP-WIRE-DOC section 2 (Limited 403, Permissive 404), not the earlier contract text.
NO-CLAIM: the sim reproduces the wire documentation, not device firmware; media-player XML, key error codes and icon bytes are FILL until sampled read-only from the real devices.
Note: the SSDP scenarios need the `sweep_to(target, mx)` seam from m7b.

comments.author: SandyOrchid
comments.text: LANG:EN Busy-retry diagnosis for Quiet 60752 (read-only, locked source): the observed loser error IS covered by the existing classifier yet still escaped. BusySnapshot displays database is busy (snapshot conflict on pages: ..) (fsqlite-error 0.4.10 lib.rs:242), which matches is_lock_contention substring (mutation.rs:264-266), so retry_on_busy (64 immediate no-sleep attempts, :248-260) did engage. SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT means the winner committed overlapping write-set pages mid-loser-txn; 64 zero-sleep spins burn in microseconds while the winner is still publishing, so bound exhaustion under a barrier-synced race is expected, not anomalous. SDK-internal busy_timeout cannot fix this: it covers lock waits (begin/commit escalation), not failed SSI validation, which needs a whole-transaction restart against a settled snapshot. Suggested direction: match the BusySnapshot variant (not the busy substring) and give it a small number of SLEPT/backoff retries instead of spins; keep plain Busy on the fast spin path. No edit attempted (Quiet-owned policy lane).

comments.author: SandyOrchid
comments.text: LANG:EN Revision to my prior busy note: downgrade diagnosis to HYPOTHESIS. Substring match on BusySnapshot proves retry_on_busy engaged only if the failing op went through try_record_with_retry; authorize_mutation_at also propagates un-retried store failures (peek_confirmation_grant, consume_confirmation_token paths), which could be the actual hard-error source - I did not trace which op failed on which attempt. Further, my 1r4.8.5 finding cuts the other way: a failed COMMIT leaves the txn active, so even genuine retries may re-execute against stale snapshot state rather than a fresh one. Needed before any backoff recommendation: instrument which operation failed, attempt counts to exhaustion, and transaction cleanup state between attempts. Do not implement slept-backoff on the exhaustion theory alone.

LANG:EN SOURCE PRE-REVIEW against current worktree at HEAD e04cf9f plus untracked fixture; no source edits, tests, builds, or runtime run.

Positive path: main.rs default info/active-app dispatch uses daemon_client; API routes call device_info/active_app; cli_daemon_mutations launches the real CLI and serve process against SimDevice, uses an empty separate client DB, parses JSON stdout, checks clean stderr, and verifies hOmE leaves app 1001 active while Home returns Roku. Current integration assertion omits this field, so it does not lock that edge.

P1 fixture isolation defect: tests/common/mutation_daemon.rs starts serve with --bind only. serve defaults no_ssdp=false and runs discover_on_startup before binding HTTP; ssdp_io::discover sends multicast and probes discovered endpoints, then serve queries apps for each discovered device. The child also inherits ZESTROKU_TARGETS. Thus this supposedly simulator-only fixture can issue ECP GETs to non-fixture LAN devices. Use a simulator-only targets file with --no-ssdp (the flag requires targets) and remove inherited target configuration before calling the fixture remote-only.

P1 privacy defect in the changed API path: routes.rs execute_mutation checks requested_app name.contains(token) case-sensitively, then stores the unmodified label in action intent. Core issue_approval emits lowercase hex tokens. An uppercase version of the presented token bypasses this guard and is reversible from the persisted label; the current test covers only the exact-case token. This is source-derived, not runtime-reproduced.

Adjacent pre-existing privacy path, not introduced by this diff: main.rs resolve_cli_target persists args.join(" ") in a local denied ActionRow for ambiguous mutation targets, including --confirm TOKEN. The canonical-IP fixture does not exercise it, so its empty-client-audit assertion is not a proof for ambiguous targets. No runtime claim.

comments.author: SandyOrchid
comments.text: LANG:EN Researched fix (no edit: file TQ-held through 10:37). Root cause: SqliteStore::in_transaction (store/mod.rs:241-256) rolls back body errors but commit errors leave via bare ? at :248. Locked fsqlite source: worker CommitTransaction just runs conn.commit_transaction() (async_api.rs:1345) with no auto-rollback wrapper; SQLite leaves the txn ACTIVE on BUSY-at-commit, so the connection stays dirty and later statements join the stale txn. Fix: on commit error, attempt rollback_transaction_sync (ignore its result), then return the ORIGINAL commit error (never mask it with the rollback outcome). Suggested shape: self.conn.commit_transaction_sync().map_err(|commit_err| { let _ = self.conn.rollback_transaction_sync(); backend(commit_err) })?. Test hook: force a commit-time BUSY (concurrent writer) and assert a subsequent independent transaction on the SAME connection succeeds with no partial rows; body-error and cleanup-failure paths stay distinguishable by their existing messages.

These are source-model observations, not runtime/product PASS.

**Principal normalization contract.** Keep transport principal separate from operation `surface`. The current CLI contexts use `client="cli"`; `mcp::decide` uses `client="mcp"` (mcp/lib.rs:104-108), and the current CLI invokes `zestroku_mcp::run_stdio` (main.rs:327; mcp/lib.rs:416-426). The related M8 policy contract names canonical principals `cli`, `mcp-stdio`, and `loopback-http`. Therefore normalize the current stdio adapter's legacy `mcp` label to `mcp-stdio` at the trusted boundary; do not infer principal from `surface` (`key`/`launch`/`install`). A future loopback HTTP mutation adapter must set `loopback-http` explicitly; there are no current HTTP POST routes. Unknown/unresolved principal remains read-only and must not snapshot, consume a confirmation, or reach a device sink.

**Corrected ordering at existing seams.** Withdraw the prior proposal to capture `before_state` after approval. `MutationContext` requires `before_state` (mutation.rs:34-40); `authorize_mutation_at` inserts the denied/approved `ActionRow` using that field (mutation.rs:92-118,154-168). Proposed shared order: (1) resolve a trusted principal and target; unknown principal is read-only; (2) run the shared core allow/rate/quiet preflight before any device read; on policy denial, write a denied action row with an explicit no-snapshot marker, without consuming a token or sending; (3) on policy permit, capture `before_state` at the caller before `authorize_mutation`, because the existing context/action insertion requires it; (4) keep existing authorization precedence—POST check, tier check, then one-use token consume/update; (5) only after approval invoke the CLI device POST sink; (6) finish the action by updating result. This distinguishes policy-preflight-before-read from snapshot-before-authorization, preserves tier-before-confirmation precedence, and leaves denied attempts auditable. MCP currently passes `before_state="unavailable (m7c wires the probe)"` and returns “dispatch happens in serve”; that approval text is not evidence of device execution. HTTP remains read-only. No source or existing policy/mutation acceptance changes are implied.

**Existing source facts preserved.** Token consumption SELECTs a valid unconsumed device/action token then UPDATEs `consumed_at` with the same guard predicates (store/mod.rs:379-396), not delete-on-match. main.rs:330-333 dispatches install separately from key/launch; install.rs:207 authorizes and later calls `installer::install`, mutate.rs:301 authorizes and later calls `send_selected`. Local token/action/alias/tier-store writes remain distinct from device POSTs. Current MCP registers key/launch only and does not dispatch; current HTTP API has no POST route.

**Future in-tree negatives — UNVERIFIED.** (1) policy denial with a valid token logs `POLICY_DENIED` but leaves `consumed_at` unchanged and sends no device request; (2) unknown principal stays read-only; (3) quiet-hours denial never bypasses per-operation confirmation. No runtime/build claim.

comments.author: PeachStork
comments.text:
LANG:EN — .11.2 startup discovery design note (review only; no source edits).

Current seam: origin/main serve.rs:45-48 registers SIGTERM then runs App startup hooks; run() opens the store at :96 and builds the shared API app at :103, with no discovery. `devices.rs:35-55,81-83,112-134` already establishes the target semantics: `ZESTROKU_TARGETS` default, `--targets` override, default `~/.config/zestroku/targets.toml` via inventory::read_seeds, `--no-ssdp` seed-only, and `--mx` 1..=5 (default 3). Reuse inventory.rs:34-70 and core ssdp_io::discover; do not add a config format, private /24 fallback, subprocess, runtime, schema, or second discovery service.

Proposed lifecycle: extend serve options only with `--targets`, `--no-ssdp`, and `--mx`; open the DB once, retain the same `Arc<Mutex<SqliteStore>>` and transport for unchanged `build_app`, and pass that same state to a small local startup step. In the existing async serve entry, register SIGTERM first, then await exactly one discovery/inventory pass before `app.run_startup_hooks` and before binding/listening. `--no-ssdp` uses `inventory::seeds_only`; otherwise call `ssdp_io::discover(transport, seeds, mx)`. Network calls occur outside the DB mutex. Persist each successful `(Device, identity)` through `inventory::persist_inventory` under a short lock; identity moves/aliases remain producer-owned. If persistence errors, fail startup before hooks/listener.

title: Bound SSDP-advertised probes to the approved discovery scope
description:
WHAT: (a) Preserve the SSDP responder source address and enforce an explicit discovery trust policy before probing any LOCATION-derived host/port. A responder must not induce the daemon to send ECP requests to loopback, metadata, unrelated private addresses, DNS names, or off-LAN targets; preserve separately operator-configured seeds and explicit scan ranges. (b) Add in-tree loopback known-bad fixtures with a valid roku:ecp response whose LOCATION escapes the allowed source/scope; assert refusal occurs before the injected Transport is called, while a valid in-scope responder remains discoverable.
WHY: The owner rule is own devices and own LAN. discovery.rs:55-69 accepts an arbitrary LOCATION authority, and ssdp_io.rs:108-110 discards recv_from source before :157-160 probes each endpoint. A LAN responder can therefore direct the daemon into an unapproved ECP GET.
ACCEPTANCE: [a] The discovery policy is explicit and enforced before Transport::send for SSDP-derived endpoints; configured seeds and explicit scan behavior remain unchanged. [b] The planted out-of-scope LOCATION test fails if validation is removed and proves zero transport calls; a valid in-scope responder is still accepted. [c] Tests cover loopback/metadata/off-LAN or DNS escape cases without contacting those destinations. [d] Exact-source remote tests and discovery/seed/scan regressions pass; no live mutation or identifier artifacts.

title: zestroku RCH pooled targets regrow ~12-21 GB per root per worker within hours and starve all Contabo workers: owner policy + measured growth
description:
WHAT: zestroku's own RCH pooled targets regrow to about 12-21 GB per root per worker within hours of building, which keeps filling every Contabo worker: contabo-1 refilled 44.1 GB free (06:40Z after reclaim) to 10.3 GB (07:39Z); contabo-4 refilled from 29.1 GB (07:47Z) to 12.9 GB (09:36Z). rch gc cannot reap them (pooled window 24 h, no flag to shorten). The reclaim route that works is native: drain, rch gc preview, apply only COLLECT, enable, probe (ompkit-wjbk, ev_c0f1ec64289a6035).
MEASURED 2026-10-13 09:36Z (rch cache status, rc 0): per worker TWO zestroku pooled stores plus a cargo cache: contabo-1: Developer/zestroku pool 16715 MB + rch-build/rch-remote/zestroku pool 21245 MB + cargo cache 1064 MB = 39025 MB, 0 reapable. contabo-4: Developer/zestroku pool 11994 MB + rch-build pool 13274 MB + cache 4897 MB = 30166 MB. contabo-2: zestroku Developer pool 6583 MB (4h idle) + others. Reading: a plain rch exec fills the Developer/zestroku pool, a clean-overlay run fills the rch-build/.../zestroku pool, so using both modes costs two pools per worker. NOT measured: growth per run, or whether pools are reused across different --base shas (an earlier guess of per-sha pools was refuted: same hash names reappeared).
WHY: contabo-1/-2/-3 sit at 0 slots on disk; contabo-4 (8 GB RAM) is the only worker that can run a job, and OOM-killed rustc three times today (kernel log, see AM 52352). Capacity is the binding constraint on every zestroku gate.
ASK (owner decision, not a code change): choose and record a policy: (1) clean-overlay only for proofs, plain runs only for scratch checks, so one pool per worker; (2) a cap or a scheduled sequenced reclaim for zestroku pools after each proof batch (sanctioned route only: drain, preview, apply COLLECT, enable, probe); (3) ask the RCH owner for a shorter pooled window or a per-project cap (rch gc has no such option today). Not proposed: deleting pools by hand, bypassing rch gc, or weakening any gate.

ROOT CAUSE MEASURED (PeachLeopard, read-only ssh at 18:40Z). contabo-1 went from 42 GB free at 17:20Z back to 8.4 GB within about 80 min. The refill is one zestroku pool, …/rch-remote/zestroku/.rch-target-contabo-1-pool-63765871…: 33 GB, of which debug/build is 32 GB (incremental only 0.76 GB). By package: zestroku-cli 16.5 GB, zestroku-api 4.4, zestroku-core 3.5, asupersync 2.7, zestroku-mcp 0.8, fsqlite-core 0.8. zestroku-cli alone has 26 unit dirs (one per integration-test binary: tests/ has 17 files, plus lib and bins), at 0.7-0.9 GB each. Example: 5ab72c6b…/out/tier_gate-… is 740 MB. So every test binary statically links the whole workspace with FULL debuginfo. The root Cargo.toml has no [profile] section, so dev/test run at debug=2. Concrete fix to measure: add to the workspace Cargo.toml
[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"
[profile.dev.package."*"]
debug = false
Line-tables-only debuginfo usually makes test binaries several times smaller and links faster, while backtraces keep file:line. Second lever, a larger change: fold the 17 integration tests into one tests/<suite>/main.rs binary, so the workspace links once instead of 17 times. Acceptance should be measured, not assumed: pool size (du -s) before and after one full 'cargo test --workspace --no-run' via rch on the same worker, plus one backtrace still showing file:line. Until this lands, deleting pools only buys about an hour (see my 17:19Z disclosure on RCHDISK1).
